clue.text: Someone acting as a stopgap

parts.note: acting is meant literally: a stage performer who steps in to fill a gap when the lead cannot appear

explanation.definitionFit: A theatre stand-in learns a role so as to perform it temporarily when the principal is absent.

clue.text: The state authorised demolition to start

indicators.note: demolition is a breaking up, so the letters taken are knocked into a new order
to start limits the fodder to the opening four letters of authorised

explanation.surface: The government gave permission for the knocking-down work to begin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to start' takes AUTH, the opening of 'authorised', and 'demolition' rearranges it. 'The state' looks like the government; it is an American one.
explanation.definitionFit: It is an example: one of the fifty American states, capital Salt Lake City.

clue.text: One sided wrangle about getting divorced

indicators.note: about puts the rearranged letters around the other piece
a wrangle is a tussle, so the letters of the word before it are thrown about

parts.note: a unit is a single one of something

explanation.surface: A lopsided argument over getting a divorce.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One sided' reads as a single phrase, lopsided, but the two words do separate jobs: 'wrangle' makes DISED, which 'about' wraps round the word for one.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are adjectives for people separated and no longer joined together.

clue.text: Hoist, as a prelude to

definitions.meaning: to raise a flag up its pole
the period leading to an event, as in the weeks before an election

explanation.definitionFit: Raising a flag and the lead-in period before an event share this phrase, the second as a noun.

clue.text: Get up to pour mine into, but it's full

indicators.note: into says the rearranged letters go inside the other piece
in a down clue, up means the word is read from bottom to top
pouring sends things flowing out of place, so the letters of mine are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone rises to pour their drink into a glass that is already full.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Get up' reads as rising from a chair; 'up' gives TEG, 'pour' gives EMIN, and 'into' nests them. 'mine' is not a possessive here, just letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A place described this way is crowded to overflowing, a synonym in 'the streets were full of people'.

clue.text: Had gone into the drink that one threw away

definitions.meaning: the drink is slang for the sea: an aircraft brought down on water
discarded or got rid of something unwanted

explanation.definitionFit: An emergency landing on the sea and discarding something both use this past-tense verb.

clue.text: Make a trap to catch

indicators.note: to catch means the trap word holds the letter inside it

parts.note: a gin is a snare for catching game

explanation.surface: Building a snare to catch an animal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Make a trap' reads as one phrase, but 'Make' alone is the definition: 'to catch' has GIN, a snare, taking in A.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym in the money sense: to make a profit is to earn one.

clue.text: What it took so long to translate

definitions.text: What it took so long to translate

parts.words: What it took so long to translate
parts.note: so long is the farewell, not a length of time: the clue wants the French word that renders it

explanation.definitionFit: The French farewell is what you get on putting the English goodbye phrase into another language.

clue.text: It's not one of the novices that's not running

definitions.text: It's not one of the novices
definitions.meaning: a whimsical reading: a novice is a beginner, so something that is not a beginner
a horse entered for a race that does not take part

explanation.definitionFit: Read whimsically it is no beginner; in racing it is an entrant withdrawn before the off.

clue.text: Mean he will be caught by, eventually

indicators.note: caught by means the second piece is held inside the first

parts.note: to mean to do something is to intend it

explanation.surface: A nasty man will finally be caught by someone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mean' wants to be an adjective for a nasty man, but it is a verb, to have in mind; 'will be caught by' is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: An adverbial phrase that is a synonym: finally, when all is done.

clue.text: A child run in for a crime

parts.note: R is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for run
a son is someone's child

explanation.surface: A youngster is arrested and brought in over an offence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'run in' reads as arrested; here R, cricket's abbreviation for run, goes 'in' SON, after A.
explanation.definitionFit: It is an example: the offence of deliberately setting fire to property.

clue.text: A number will be pulling out

definitions.meaning: an internal telephone line reached by its own digits
the act of stretching or drawing something out longer

explanation.definitionFit: An office telephone line has its own digits, and lengthening something by drawing it out is the same noun.

clue.text: An irritable "bite? Fiddle-de-Dee!"

parts.note: a dog that snaps bites suddenly
pish, like fiddle-de-dee, is an old exclamation of contempt meaning nonsense

explanation.surface: A grumpy person scoffs at the offer of something to eat.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: short-tempered and inclined to speak sharply.

clue.text: Meet outside a hangout

indicators.note: outside says the word for meet goes around the letter

parts.note: a meet is the gathering of riders and hounds for a fox hunt in Britain

explanation.surface: Arranging to see someone in front of a favourite gathering place.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Meet' is the noun: in Britain a meet is the assembly of a fox HUNT, which here goes 'outside' A.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: a place someone frequents regularly.

clue.text: Having had a go at police unfairly, is sorry

indicators.note: unfairly suggests things not done straight, so the letters of the three words are disordered

explanation.surface: Someone who wrongly criticised the police now regrets it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unfairly' rearranges GO, AT and POLICE; 'had a go at' reads as criticised, hiding the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: expressing regret for a wrong done.

clue.text: Setting in competition against and giving marks to

definitions.meaning: matching one's strength or wits against an opponent
making small dents or scars in a surface

explanation.definitionFit: Matching rivals against each other and scarring a surface with small hollows share this participle.

clue.text: He's high-minded and that's perfect at first

parts.note: ideal means perfect, the best imaginable
first written with figures is 1st, and the figure 1 is read as the letter I

explanation.surface: A principled man who seems flawless when you first meet him.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at first' looks like a signal to take an opening letter. It is not: first is written in figures, 1st, and the digit is read as a capital letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A person guided by lofty principles rather than practical considerations.

clue.text: It has shelves he's putting his things on

definitions.meaning: a kitchen sideboard with open racks above for plates
things are clothes: a person getting clothed

explanation.definitionFit: A kitchen sideboard with racks for plates, and whimsically a person who is getting clothed.

clue.text: A number (less easily explained) shielding the killer

indicators.note: shielding means the longer word covers the letter, holding it inside

parts.note: stranger means odder, harder to account for
L is the Roman numeral for fifty

explanation.surface: A witness's phone number is kept back to protect a murderer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shielding' puts L, the Roman fifty, inside STRANGER.
explanation.definitionFit: It is an example: a murderer who kills by throttling.

clue.text: Runs back angry and the boys catch it!

indicators.note: catch has the word for boys taking the other piece inside

parts.note: lads are boys

indicators.note: back means the word for angry is written right to left

parts.note: someone red with rage is angry

explanation.surface: A furious person chases back after some lads, who are in for it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns RED into DER, which LADS 'catch'. 'Runs' is a noun: the lines of unravelled stitches in tights.
explanation.definitionFit: In British usage, runs in stockings or tights are called this, from their rung-like look.

clue.text: A house is engulfed by the flood: awful misfortune

indicators.note: engulfed by means the first piece is swallowed inside the second

parts.note: a surge is a sudden rush of water
a house is a business firm, a company, abbreviated Co

explanation.surface: A home is swallowed by floodwater, a terrible disaster.
explanation.walkthrough: 'house' is a business house, a company, CO, which 'is engulfed by' SURGE.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: something that causes great suffering, an affliction or plague.

clue.text: In other words, needs to tear round to validate

indicators.note: round says the rearranged letters go around the short word
tearing something rips it apart, so the letters of needs are rearranged

parts.note: or introduces an alternative way of putting something

explanation.surface: Put another way, someone must rush about to get a document approved.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to tear round' reads as one phrase, rushing about, but splits into two signals: 'to tear' makes ENDSE and 'round' is the container.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: to give official approval to something, such as signing a cheque.

clue.text: Having changed key fixed things

parts.note: E is a musical key
someone who fixed things mended them

explanation.surface: After swapping the key, someone repaired things.
explanation.walkthrough: 'key' looks like a door key or a swapped lock; it is the musical key E.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym for text that has been corrected or altered.

clue.text: Question the guard

definitions.meaning: to interrogate someone closely
a protective metal lattice over a window or radiator

explanation.definitionFit: To interrogate closely, and a protective lattice of metal bars.

clue.text: No good at all in the point-to-point

parts.note: East is a point of the compass, abbreviated E
East is a point of the compass, abbreviated E

explanation.surface: A hopeless horse or rider in an amateur steeplechase.
explanation.walkthrough: A point-to-point is a British amateur horse race across country; here it gives E, a compass point, running on to PT.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: clumsy and wholly lacking in skill.

clue.text: Making plain to one by innuendo

parts.note: overt means open and plain to see
taken as written

explanation.surface: Getting a message across to somebody through sly hints.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is a deliberate contradiction, making things clear by hinting. 'Making' and 'by' only join the parts.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: a subtle implied meaning beneath what is said.

clue.text: When one's running, splits

definitions.meaning: what one does when rushing along at great speed
rips or comes apart

explanation.definitionFit: Someone rushing along at speed does this, and so does cloth that rips.

clue.text: Bear up when there's a delay

definitions.meaning: to prop or support something
a postponement, as of a court's sentence

explanation.definitionFit: To prop or support, and a legal postponement such as one of execution.

clue.text: Prized, take a certain step to protect

indicators.note: to protect means the word for step wraps round the other, sheltering it

parts.note: to tread is to step
sure means certain

explanation.surface: Someone takes a particular measure to safeguard a valued possession.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a certain step' reads as some particular measure, but the adjective and the noun are separate pieces, and 'to protect' is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: valued highly and cherished.

clue.text: Would give a great deal to hear

indicators.note: to hear says the phrase is taken by its sound rather than its spelling

parts.note: a lot means a great deal, a large amount

explanation.surface: Someone would pay dearly to listen to something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to hear' asks for what 'a lot' sounds like, spelt as a different word.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: to assign or hand out a share to someone.

clue.text: Is not the dealer, but gets commissions

definitions.meaning: at cards, the player who divides the pack before the dealer deals
shares of the takings paid to a go-between

explanation.definitionFit: At cards another player divides the pack for whoever deals; a share of takings is the same word.

clue.text: "Metal in the form of a salver" does fool you

parts.note: lead is a heavy metal
as means in the form or guise of
a salver is a serving tray

explanation.surface: A serving dish that looks like solid silver turns out to deceive you.
explanation.walkthrough: The three pieces run together and the word breaks then fall in different places, 4,6, to give the phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: To deceive someone is to guide them into error, a near synonym.
